phases.purpose: Design controlled experiments and generative systems with rigorous statistical baselines.

phases.name: Scaled Systems & LLMs

phases.purpose: Scale training to clusters and engineer agentic, retrieval-augmented systems.

levels.title: Scientific Computing & Python
levels.scope: Build the foundational computing, Linux shell, Python programming, unit testing, and containerized laboratory environment setup required to conduct reproducible research without relying on tutorial code.
levels.prereqStated: None; designed for a complete beginner entering scientific computing

modules.name: Command-Line Foundations, Linux Shell & Remote Laboratory Work

objectives.text: Prerequisites & Foundations: Explain how operating systems coordinate processes, memory, file descriptors, and remote network streams during scientific computation.
objectives.group: Linux filesystem, shell navigation & process control

objectives.text: Command-Line Operations: Navigate Linux filesystems, manage process priority with nice, inspect resource usage with htop, and manage background execution with tmux.
objectives.group: Linux filesystem, shell navigation & process control

objectives.text: Remote Laboratory Access: Configure SSH key pairs, edit ssh config files, manage persistent remote sessions, and transfer datasets with rsync and scp.
objectives.group: Remote server workflows, SSH & credential security

objectives.text: Security & Credential Hygiene: Isolate credentials in non-committed environment variables, configure gitignore, and sanitize secret keys from terminal history.
objectives.group: Remote server workflows, SSH & credential security

modules.mentalModel: The terminal is an exact scientific instrument; every command should be predictable, auditable, and documented in your laboratory log.
modules.tryIt: Set up a remote Linux virtual machine or container, configure SSH keys, create a project directory hierarchy, and transfer a sample dataset using rsync.
modules.outcome: You can independently navigate Linux environments, manage background computing jobs, and execute remote laboratory tasks securely.
modules.evidence: Set up a remote Linux virtual machine or container, configure SSH keys, create a project directory hierarchy, and transfer a sample dataset using rsync.

modules.name: Research-Grade Python Programming & Memory-Aware Vectorization

objectives.text: Core Language Mechanics: Write idiomatic Python using list and dictionary comprehensions, generators, custom iterators, and immutable data structures.
objectives.group: Data structures, functional programming & type safety

objectives.text: Type Annotations & Clean Code: Apply type hints with typing and dataclasses, document functions with NumPy-style docstrings, and enforce static verification with mypy.
objectives.group: Data structures, functional programming & type safety

objectives.text: Memory Layout & Strides: Understand contiguous memory layouts (C-order vs Fortran-order), tensor dimensions, array slicing, and avoid slow Python-level loops.
Broadcasting & Numerical Verification: Master array broadcasting rules, vector operations, and compare hand-derived calculations against vectorized implementations.

modules.mentalModel: Scientific Python is not just syntax; it is the discipline of mapping abstract mathematical operations into memory-efficient, cache-friendly vector instructions.
modules.tryIt: Implement a multi-dimensional Euclidean pairwise distance matrix from scratch using pure Python loops, then reimplement it with NumPy broadcasting and measure the 50x speedup.
modules.outcome: You can write robust, vectorized, and type-annotated Python code suitable for scientific research workflows.
modules.evidence: Implement a multi-dimensional Euclidean pairwise distance matrix from scratch using pure Python loops, then reimplement it with NumPy broadcasting and measure the 50x speedup.

modules.name: Software Engineering for Researchers: Testing, Debugging & Profiling

objectives.text: Test-Driven Research Habits: Write parameterized unit tests with pytest to verify numerical edge cases, empty datasets, and invalid feature dimensions.
Property-Based Testing: Use hypothesis to generate random inputs and verify mathematical invariants such as matrix symmetry, non-negativity, and triangle inequality.
Interactive Debugging: Step through failing execution graphs using pdb and breakpoint, inspecting stack frames, local variables, and tensor shapes.
Computational Profiling: Profile code bottlenecks using cProfile and line_profiler to isolate memory allocations and expensive subroutines before training models.

modules.mentalModel: A research script without automated unit tests is an uncalibrated measuring tool whose experimental outputs cannot be trusted.
modules.tryIt: Write a data preprocessing function with five deliberate edge-case failures, then write a pytest suite that catches each failure and asserts proper exception handling.
modules.outcome: You can systematically debug, profile, and unit-test scientific Python code to ensure software correctness.
modules.evidence: Write a data preprocessing function with five deliberate edge-case failures, then write a pytest suite that catches each failure and asserts proper exception handling.

modules.name: Version Control, Experiment Logs & Lab Notebooks

objectives.text: Version Control Disciplines: Initialize Git repositories, write conventional atomic commit messages, and manage branches for distinct experimental hypotheses.
objectives.group: Git branching models for empirical research

objectives.text: Collaborative Workflows: Submit pull requests, conduct peer code reviews on research implementations, and diff Jupyter notebooks cleanly using nbdime.
objectives.group: Git branching models for empirical research

objectives.text: Laboratory Notebook Keeping: Maintain a dated research log recording hypothesis motivations, hardware configurations, exact random seeds, and failed attempts.
Provenance Tracking: Bind Git commit hashes and parameter dictionaries to every generated figure, table, and checkpoint file to guarantee full auditability.

modules.mentalModel: A scientific Git history is the legal record of your experimental reasoning, preserving every hypothesis and decision made during a study.
modules.tryIt: Publish an open-source research template repository on GitHub with clean branch history, automated GitHub Actions CI, and an informative README.
modules.outcome: You can manage research software collaboratively with Git and maintain complete provenance across experimental iterations.
modules.evidence: Publish an open-source research template repository on GitHub with clean branch history, automated GitHub Actions CI, and an informative README.

modules.name: Environment Locking, Containerization & Artifact Reproducibility

objectives.text: Package Isolation: Configure isolated environments with uv or conda, specifying exact Python minor versions and system-level dependencies.
Deterministic Lockfiles: Generate frozen lockfiles (pyproject.toml or conda-lock) that pin package hashes and wheel builds to prevent dependency drift.
Docker Containerization: Write reproducible multi-stage Dockerfiles specifying base CUDA drivers, non-root user permissions, and entrypoint scripts.
HPC Container Portability: Build Singularity/Apptainer images for high-performance computing clusters where root container execution is restricted.

modules.mentalModel: Software reproducibility means another researcher on a different continent and operating system can reproduce your exact computational environment in one command.
modules.tryIt: Containerize a Python numerical benchmark using Docker, mount a local data directory, run the script inside the container, and verify identical outputs.
modules.outcome: You can build, lock, and containerize reproducible research environments across workstations and shared compute clusters.
modules.evidence: Containerize a Python numerical benchmark using Docker, mount a local data directory, run the script inside the container, and verify identical outputs.

modules.name: Capstone: Reproducible Research Laboratory Environment & Experiment Harness

objectives.text: Build a modular, object-oriented experiment harness featuring decoupled configuration parsing, automated smoke testing, and deterministic seeding.
Integrate automated CLI argument validation, system metrics logging (CPU/RAM/GPU memory), and clean output directory structuring (data, logs, figures).
Package the entire experimental harness inside a Docker container with an automated Makefile and comprehensive documentation.
Execute a full smoke test from a clean environment on a secondary machine, verifying that outputs match bit-for-bit with stored golden artifacts.

modules.finalResult: A fully reproducible, tested, and containerized research laboratory harness that serves as the foundation for all subsequent machine learning studies.
modules.evidence: A fully reproducible, tested, and containerized research laboratory harness that serves as the foundation for all subsequent machine learning studies.

levels.title: Mathematical Foundations
levels.scope: Master the linear algebra, multivariable vector calculus, matrix differentials, convex optimization, and first-order algorithms essential for deriving and analyzing AI/ML models from scratch.

modules.name: Vector Spaces, Linear Independence, Projections & Decompositions

objectives.text: Prerequisites & Foundations: Define vector spaces, subspaces, linear independence, basis, span, dimension, inner products, and orthogonality in Euclidean space.
Geometry & Projections: Compute vector projections onto subspaces, orthogonal complements, and execute Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization with geometric visualization.
Matrix Algebra: Connect matrix multiplication to linear transformations, change of basis, kernel/nullspace, and the Rank-Nullity Theorem.
Matrix Decompositions: Formulate Eigendecomposition of symmetric matrices, Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), spectral norm, and low-rank matrix approximations.

modules.mentalModel: High-dimensional data points are vectors in geometric spaces; matrix transformations rotate, scale, and project this geometry into lower dimensions.
modules.tryIt: Implement SVD from scratch using the power iteration method for top singular vectors and verify against NumPy linalg svd on an image compression task.
modules.outcome: You can manipulate high-dimensional geometric spaces, compute matrix decompositions, and derive low-rank approximations analytically.
modules.evidence: Implement SVD from scratch using the power iteration method for top singular vectors and verify against NumPy linalg svd on an image compression task.

modules.name: Multivariable Vector Calculus & Matrix Differential Calculus

objectives.text: Multivariable Differentiation: Compute partial derivatives, directional derivatives, gradient vectors, Jacobian matrices, and Hessian curvature matrices.
Multivariate Taylor Expansions: Construct first-order and second-order Taylor approximations to analyze local curvature and function approximations near stationary points.
Matrix Calculus Rules: Derive gradients of scalar loss functions with respect to vectors and matrices using numerator layout conventions and trace tricks.
Computation Graphs & Autograd: Trace forward-mode and reverse-mode automatic differentiation on directed graphs, calculating vector-Jacobian products (VJPs).

modules.mentalModel: Matrix calculus allows us to calculate sensitivity across thousands of interacting parameters simultaneously along the tangent spaces of error surfaces.
modules.tryIt: Derive the analytical matrix gradient of a two-layer linear autoencoder loss function and verify the computation graph gradient with two-sided numerical finite differences.
modules.outcome: You can calculate complex matrix derivatives, trace computational graphs, and verify analytical gradients numerically.
modules.evidence: Derive the analytical matrix gradient of a two-layer linear autoencoder loss function and verify the computation graph gradient with two-sided numerical finite differences.

modules.name: Convex Optimization Theory, Duality & Constraints

objectives.text: Convexity Analysis: Identify convex sets, convex functions, affine hulls, epigraphs, and apply Jensen's inequality to establish mathematical bounds.
Non-Smooth Optimization: Formulate subgradients and subdifferentials for non-differentiable points such as ReLU activations and L1-norm penalties.
Constrained Formulations: Formulate primal optimization problems with inequality and equality constraints using Lagrange multipliers.
objectives.group: Constrained optimization, Lagrangian duality & KKT conditions

objectives.text: Duality & Optimality: Derive the Lagrange dual function, prove weak and strong duality under Slater's condition, and solve Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions.
objectives.group: Constrained optimization, Lagrangian duality & KKT conditions

modules.mentalModel: Convexity guarantees that any local minimum is a global minimum, providing rigorous theoretical guarantees for machine learning convergence.
modules.tryIt: Derive the Wolfe dual formulation and KKT conditions for a soft-margin Support Vector Machine by hand and solve the quadratic program using an analytical toy example.
modules.outcome: You can determine function convexity, formulate Lagrangian duals, and apply KKT optimality conditions to constrained ML problems.
modules.evidence: Derive the Wolfe dual formulation and KKT conditions for a soft-margin Support Vector Machine by hand and solve the quadratic program using an analytical toy example.

modules.name: First-Order & Adaptive Optimization Algorithms

objectives.text: Gradient Descent Dynamics: Analyze convergence rates of Batch Gradient Descent, Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD), and mini-batch SGD on convex and non-convex surfaces.
Accelerated Methods: Implement classical momentum and Nesterov Accelerated Gradient (NAG) to dampen oscillations along high-curvature ravines.
Adaptive Optimizers: Derive and compare AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adam, and AdamW (decoupled weight decay) to handle sparse gradients and ill-conditioned curvatures.
objectives.group: Adaptive learning rate optimizers & weight decay

objectives.text: Numerical Stability: Implement numerical guards including the log-sum-exp trick for stable softmax calculations, gradient clipping, and condition number audits.
objectives.group: Adaptive learning rate optimizers & weight decay

modules.mentalModel: Optimization is navigation across a high-dimensional loss terrain; adaptive algorithms adjust step sizes along each coordinate based on past gradient variance.
modules.tryIt: Build a simulation notebook comparing SGD, Momentum, RMSProp, and AdamW on ill-conditioned quadratic surfaces and the Rosenbrock function, tracking convergence steps.
modules.outcome: You can select, implement, and tune first-order and adaptive optimizers while diagnosing numerical instability and ill-conditioning.
modules.evidence: Build a simulation notebook comparing SGD, Momentum, RMSProp, and AdamW on ill-conditioned quadratic surfaces and the Rosenbrock function, tracking convergence steps.

modules.name: Paper Reading & Theoretical Verification in Optimization

objectives.text: Seminal Paper Reading: Study Boyd & Vandenberghe (Convex Optimization), Kingma & Ba (Adam, 2014), and Loshchilov & Hutter (Decoupled Weight Decay / AdamW, 2017).
Research Questions: Investigate why L2 regularization fails in Adam without explicit decoupling, and how learning rate warmups stabilize early training dynamics.
Analytical Verification: Write automated finite-difference gradient checkers to validate analytical derivations against numerical approximations (|f'(x) - f_num(x)| < 1e-6).
Optimization Ablations: Design an ablation comparing Adam with L2 regularization versus AdamW on generalization performance and parameter weight distributions.

modules.mentalModel: Reading optimization papers requires checking their mathematical proofs against numerical simulations to verify where assumptions hold or break.
modules.tryIt: Replicate the core empirical finding of the AdamW paper on a small neural network, demonstrating that AdamW yields superior weight decay dynamics than standard Adam with L2 penalty.
modules.outcome: You can critically read optimization literature, reproduce theoretical claims, and perform rigorous numerical verification.
modules.evidence: Replicate the core empirical finding of the AdamW paper on a small neural network, demonstrating that AdamW yields superior weight decay dynamics than standard Adam with L2 penalty.

modules.name: Capstone: Numerical Optimization Engine & Convex Solver from Scratch

objectives.text: Build a standalone, object-oriented numerical optimization library in pure NumPy containing SGD with Nesterov momentum, AdamW, and L-BFGS.
objectives.group: Architecture of a standalone numerical optimization solver

objectives.text: Implement an automated computation graph engine supporting scalar and tensor automatic differentiation with reverse-mode vector-Jacobian products.
objectives.group: Architecture of a standalone numerical optimization solver

objectives.text: Benchmark the solver across convex and non-convex test surfaces (Beale, Rosenbrock, Rastrigin), recording convergence rates, trajectory plots, and condition numbers.
Write a formal 4-page mathematical technical report documenting the derivation, convergence proofs, numerical verification checks, and experimental results.

modules.finalResult: A fully functional, mathematically verified numerical optimization engine written from scratch, accompanied by a rigorous technical report and benchmark suite.
modules.evidence: A fully functional, mathematically verified numerical optimization engine written from scratch, accompanied by a rigorous technical report and benchmark suite.

levels.title: Probability & Statistics
levels.scope: Master probability theory, statistical estimation, hypothesis testing, uncertainty quantification, non-parametric statistics, and multiple comparison corrections for rigorous scientific claims.

modules.name: Probability Spaces, Random Variables & Probability Distributions

objectives.text: Probability Axioms: Formulate sample spaces, events, Kolmogorov's axioms of probability, joint distributions, marginalization, and conditional probability.
Bayesian Inference Foundations: Apply Bayes' Theorem to update prior beliefs into posterior distributions given empirical likelihood observations.
Discrete & Continuous Distributions: Characterize Bernoulli, Binomial, Poisson, Gaussian/Normal, Beta, Dirichlet, Gamma, and Student's t distributions.
Moments & Expectation: Calculate expectation, variance, covariance matrices, skewness, kurtosis, and derive properties using Moment Generating Functions (MGFs).

modules.mentalModel: Probability models quantify our uncertainty about the world before data is observed, providing mathematical structures to interpret empirical phenomena.
modules.tryIt: Implement a probability distribution workbench in Python that fits parametric distributions to skewed real-world data and evaluates goodness-of-fit via QQ-plots.
modules.outcome: You can formalize uncertain processes with appropriate probability distributions and derive analytical expectations and variances.
modules.evidence: Implement a probability distribution workbench in Python that fits parametric distributions to skewed real-world data and evaluates goodness-of-fit via QQ-plots.

modules.name: Information Theory, Entropy & Divergence Measures

objectives.text: Information Measures: Define self-information, Shannon entropy for discrete variables, and differential entropy for continuous distributions.
Mutual Information: Compute joint entropy, conditional entropy, and mutual information to quantify non-linear dependencies between random variables.
Relative Entropy: Derive Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, prove non-negativity via Jensen's inequality, and analyze asymmetric information geometry.
Symmetric Metrics: Compare cross-entropy loss, Jensen-Shannon divergence, and Wasserstein distance for measuring statistical distance between probability densities.

modules.mentalModel: Entropy measures the inherent surprise or information content of a distribution; divergence measures the informational cost of approximating reality.
modules.tryIt: Code an interactive information theory visualizer calculating KL divergence between two multivariate Gaussians as their covariance matrices shift.
modules.outcome: You can apply information-theoretic metrics to measure distribution divergence, loss functions, and non-linear feature dependencies.
modules.evidence: Code an interactive information theory visualizer calculating KL divergence between two multivariate Gaussians as their covariance matrices shift.

modules.name: Point Estimation, Maximum Likelihood & Bayesian Estimation

objectives.text: Likelihood Principles: Formulate likelihood and log-likelihood functions for Gaussian and Bernoulli models; derive analytical and numerical MLE parameters.
Estimator Properties: Prove unbiasedness, asymptotic consistency, efficiency, Fisher Information, and the Cramér-Rao Lower Bound.
Bayesian Point Estimation: Formulate Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) estimation, connecting Gaussian priors to L2 weight decay and Laplace priors to L1 penalties.
Conjugate Priors: Derive analytical posterior updates using conjugate prior pairs (Beta-Binomial, Dirichlet-Multinomial, Normal-Normal).

modules.mentalModel: Point estimation searches for parameter values that make observed data most probable, balanced against prior regularizing constraints.
modules.tryIt: Derive the MLE and MAP estimates for a linear regression model from first principles, code both solutions in NumPy, and verify that MAP regularizes noisy coefficients.
modules.outcome: You can formulate, derive, and analyze Maximum Likelihood and Bayesian Maximum A Posteriori estimators for arbitrary statistical models.
modules.evidence: Derive the MLE and MAP estimates for a linear regression model from first principles, code both solutions in NumPy, and verify that MAP regularizes noisy coefficients.

modules.name: Hypothesis Testing, Non-Parametric Statistics & Power Analysis

objectives.text: Hypothesis Frameworks: Formulate Null and Alternative Hypotheses (H0, H1), define Type I error rate (alpha) and Type II error rate (beta).
Parametric Tests: Execute Student's t-test, paired t-test, and ANOVA, verifying normality via Shapiro-Wilk and homoscedasticity via Levene's test.
Non-Parametric Benchmarking: Execute the Wilcoxon signed-rank test and Mann-Whitney U test on algorithm comparisons without assuming normal distributions.
Multiple Testing Adjustments: Control Family-Wise Error Rate (FWER) with Bonferroni and Holm-Bonferroni, and control False Discovery Rate (FDR) with Benjamini-Hochberg.
Statistical Power & Effect Sizes: Conduct a priori power calculations to determine necessary sample sizes and report Cohen's d alongside p-values.

modules.mentalModel: A p-value is not a measure of effect size or importance; statistical rigor requires reporting effect magnitudes, confidence bounds, and sample power.
modules.tryIt: Simulate a multi-model benchmark experiment with 10 competing algorithms across 20 datasets, apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, and detect false discovery spikes.
modules.outcome: You can design statistically sound benchmark evaluations, select appropriate non-parametric tests, and apply rigorous multiplicity adjustments.
modules.evidence: Simulate a multi-model benchmark experiment with 10 competing algorithms across 20 datasets, apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, and detect false discovery spikes.

modules.name: Resampling, Bootstrap Confidence Intervals & Conformal Prediction

objectives.text: Non-Parametric Bootstrap: Generate empirical bootstrap sampling distributions to construct 95% BCa (bias-corrected accelerated) confidence intervals for non-linear metrics.
Permutation Tests: Execute two-sample permutation tests to determine whether performance differences between two models could arise purely by chance.
Conformal Prediction Principles: Formulate non-conformity scores and construct prediction intervals with distribution-free, finite-sample marginal coverage guarantees (1 - alpha).
Uncertainty Calibration: Evaluate predictive interval width versus coverage trade-offs on regression and classification benchmarks.

modules.mentalModel: Bootstrapping allows us to quantify parameter and metric uncertainty directly from data without making unrealistic Gaussian assumptions.
modules.tryIt: Implement a bootstrap confidence interval calculator for F1-score and AUROC on an imbalanced classification test set and compare against naive normal approximations.
modules.outcome: You can compute distribution-free confidence intervals via bootstrapping and construct guaranteed prediction intervals using conformal prediction.
modules.evidence: Implement a bootstrap confidence interval calculator for F1-score and AUROC on an imbalanced classification test set and compare against naive normal approximations.

modules.name: Capstone: Statistical Rigor & Hypothesis Testing Audit Package

objectives.text: Build a Python library providing automated hypothesis testing (paired Wilcoxon, Mann-Whitney, Friedman test with Nemenyi post-hoc).
objectives.group: Engineering a comprehensive statistical evaluation toolkit

objectives.text: Integrate non-parametric bootstrap confidence interval estimation (percentile and BCa), Cohen's d effect sizes, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR adjustments.
objectives.group: Engineering a comprehensive statistical evaluation toolkit

objectives.text: Run an empirical audit on a published machine learning benchmark table, identifying uncorrected p-values, reporting true confidence intervals, and verifying statistical significance.
Produce a publication-ready LaTeX table and statistical significance critical difference diagram (Demšar plot).

modules.finalResult: An open-source, automated statistical testing and uncertainty audit package suitable for evaluating and reporting empirical AI/ML research benchmarks.
modules.evidence: An open-source, automated statistical testing and uncertainty audit package suitable for evaluating and reporting empirical AI/ML research benchmarks.

levels.title: Research Literacy & Gaps
levels.scope: Master the methodology of scholarly literature search, critical paper reading, taxonomy synthesis, research gap identification, hypothesis formulation, and preregistered proposal authoring.

modules.name: Systematic Literature Search & Bibliographic Management

objectives.text: Academic Database Architecture: Execute advanced boolean and keyword search queries across arXiv, Google Scholar, Semantic Scholar, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and PubMed.
objectives.group: Scholarly search engines & structured bibliographic querying

objectives.text: Search String Formulation: Construct reproducible search strings combining MeSH terms, ACM CCS concepts, wildcards, and explicit field tags (ti, ab, auth).
objectives.group: Scholarly search engines & structured bibliographic querying

objectives.text: Citation Graph Traversal: Trace forward citations, backward references, and co-citation networks using Connected Papers, Litmaps, and ResearchRabbit.
Reference Management: Organize references in Zotero, automate metadata extraction from DOIs, generate standardized BibTeX citation keys, and manage LaTeX bibliographies.

modules.mentalModel: A literature search is an exhaustive empirical query across the global scientific record; missing relevant prior work invalidates claims of novelty.
modules.tryIt: Build a standardized search string for an open machine learning topic, retrieve 50 candidate papers across three databases, and export an annotated BibTeX file.
modules.outcome: You can systematically discover scholarly literature, navigate citation graphs, and maintain an organized BibTeX reference repository.
modules.evidence: Build a standardized search string for an open machine learning topic, retrieve 50 candidate papers across three databases, and export an annotated BibTeX file.

modules.name: Critical Paper Reading: The Three-Pass Method & Taxonomy Synthesis

objectives.text: First Pass (Bird's Eye): Read title, abstract, section headings, and conclusions in 10 minutes to categorize the paper type, context, and core contribution.
Second Pass (Grasp Content): Examine figures, tables, mathematical formulations, and experimental setups, marking unverified assertions and missing baselines.
Third Pass (Deep Dissection): Mentally reconstruct the paper from scratch, identifying hidden assumptions, missing hyperparameters, and potential failure modes.
Evidence Auditing: Extract claims, dataset characteristics, evaluation metrics, and reported limitations into a structured Claim-Evidence-Limitation Matrix.
Methodological Taxonomy: Synthesize competing papers into an overarching taxonomy tree categorizing approaches by inductive biases, objectives, and compute budgets.

modules.mentalModel: A scientific paper is not an authoritative textbook; it is a persuasive argument supported by empirical evidence that must be cross-examined with skepticism.
modules.tryIt: Read a landmark AI paper using the Three-Pass Method, construct a Claim-Evidence Matrix, and identify two unstated assumptions or potential baseline weaknesses.
modules.outcome: You can critically evaluate scientific manuscripts in under an hour and organize competing literature into rigorous methodological taxonomies.
modules.evidence: Read a landmark AI paper using the Three-Pass Method, construct a Claim-Evidence Matrix, and identify two unstated assumptions or potential baseline weaknesses.

modules.name: Identifying Research Gaps & Scoping Original Contributions

objectives.text: Gap Typology: Distinguish genuine research gaps (contradictory empirical findings, untested distribution shifts, compute bottlenecks) from trivial engineering deltas.
objectives.group: The anatomy of genuine scientific research gaps

objectives.text: Questioning Unstated Assumptions: Interrogate foundational assumptions in current state-of-the-art methods (e.g. i.i.d. data, stationary distributions, infinite compute).
objectives.group: The anatomy of genuine scientific research gaps

objectives.text: Delta Analysis Framework: Formalize the exact difference between the state-of-the-art and your proposed idea across architecture, loss, efficiency, and guarantees.
Research Scope Bounding: Narrow a broad research interest into a feasible, high-impact investigation that can be completed within available computational and time budgets.

modules.mentalModel: Great research does not invent problems; it discovers unresolved tensions, contradictory findings, or unexamined assumptions in existing literature.
modules.tryIt: Conduct a Delta Analysis comparing three recent papers in a specific subfield, author a 1-page gap analysis, and articulate one high-leverage question they leave unresolved.
modules.outcome: You can identify legitimate research gaps in published literature and scope an original, feasible contribution.
modules.evidence: Conduct a Delta Analysis comparing three recent papers in a specific subfield, author a 1-page gap analysis, and articulate one high-leverage question they leave unresolved.

modules.name: Formulating Research Questions, Hypotheses & Preregistration

objectives.text: Question Formulation: Transform vague research goals into precise, measurable, and falsifiable Research Questions (RQ1: Efficacy, RQ2: Efficiency, RQ3: Generalization).
Hypothesis Operationalization: Define the Null Hypothesis (H0) and Alternative Hypothesis (H1), establishing clear quantitative criteria for hypothesis rejection.
Study Design Rigor: Separate confirmatory hypothesis testing from post-hoc exploratory data mining to eliminate confirmation bias and HARKing (Hypothesizing After Results are Known).
objectives.group: Confirmatory vs exploratory studies & OSF preregistration

objectives.text: Open Science Preregistration: Write a formal study preregistration protocol on the Open Science Framework (OSF) specifying primary metrics, baselines, and stopping rules.
objectives.group: Confirmatory vs exploratory studies & OSF preregistration

modules.mentalModel: If an experiment cannot fail or disprove your initial hypothesis, it is not an experiment—it is a demonstration.
modules.tryIt: Author a preregistered study plan on OSF for a proposed model comparison, specifying primary metrics, minimum effect size, random seeds, and statistical test protocols.
modules.outcome: You can formulate falsifiable research questions, operationalize testable hypotheses, and author formal study preregistrations.
modules.evidence: Author a preregistered study plan on OSF for a proposed model comparison, specifying primary metrics, minimum effect size, random seeds, and statistical test protocols.

modules.name: Research Ethics, Authorship Governance & Responsible Conduct

objectives.text: Institutional Governance: Determine when an AI study requires Institutional Review Board (IRB) human-subjects approval (e.g. crowdsourced evaluations, medical data).
Dual-Use & Societal Impact: Evaluate dual-use research of concern (DURC), potential malicious misuse, security vulnerabilities, and societal harms.
Scientific Authorship Standards: Apply ICMJE and IEEE guidelines to determine authorship versus acknowledgments, eliminating honorary or gift authorship.
objectives.group: Authorship criteria, CRediT taxonomy & conflicts of interest

objectives.text: CRediT Taxonomy: Assign transparent contributor roles (Conceptualization, Methodology, Software, Validation, Formal Analysis, Writing) and disclose funding sources and conflicts.
objectives.group: Authorship criteria, CRediT taxonomy & conflicts of interest

modules.mentalModel: Scientific integrity is the foundational currency of research; ethical shortcuts compromise personal credibility and the reproducibility of the scientific record.
modules.tryIt: Complete an ethics and reproducibility self-audit for a proposed AI study, documenting data consent protocols, compute footprint disclosures, and a CRediT contributor matrix.
modules.outcome: You can navigate research ethics, ensure regulatory and IRB compliance, and govern authorship according to international scientific standards.

Regularization Techniques: Implement inverted Dropout, Weight Decay (L2 penalty), Stochastic Depth (DropPath), and label smoothing to prevent overfitting.
Optimization Schedules: Implement Cosine Annealing with linear warmup, OneCycleLR, ReduceLROnPlateau, and gradient norm clipping.

modules.mentalModel: Training deep neural networks is the stabilization of a high-dimensional dynamical system; proper initialization and normalization keep signal variances within healthy bounds.

modules.name: Scientific Methodology, Variables & Factorial Experimental Design

objectives.text: Variable Identification: Isolate independent variables (model components, hyperparameters), dependent variables (task metrics, efficiency), and control nuisance variables.
objectives.group: Principles of scientific control in AI research

objectives.group: Principles of scientific control in AI research

modules.name: Fair Baselines, Compute Parity & Hyperparameter Optimization

objectives.text: Compute Budget Parity: Equalize total computational resources (FLOPs, wall-clock hours, or hyperparameter trial counts) across all competing baseline models.
objectives.group: The baseline fairness crisis in AI literature

objectives.text: Search Algorithms: Compare Random Search against Bayesian Optimization using Gaussian Processes and Tree-structured Parzen Estimators (TPE via Optuna).

modules.name: Ablation Study Design & Component Isolation

objectives.text: Destructive Ablations: Remove components one by one from the full proposed system to measure the unique performance degradation attributable to each isolated mechanism.
Constructive Ablations: Add proposed components step-by-step onto the minimal baseline to verify cumulative, monotonic improvements.
Architectural Ablations: Measure impact of removing skip connections, varying layer counts, disabling attention heads, and swapping normalization layers.
Objective & Loss Ablations: Evaluate contribution of auxiliary losses, contrastive penalties, and loss weighting coefficients (lambda_1, lambda_2).
Data Scaling Ablations: Evaluate performance curves across training data subsamples (1%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 100%) to test sample efficiency claims.

modules.mentalModel: An ablation study is an autopsy of your model that proves which specific parts of your proposed method actually drive the claimed empirical gains.

modules.name: Variational Autoencoders (VAE) & Latent Variable Models

objectives.text: Intractable Posteriors: Formulate generative latent variable models p(x, z), explain the intractability of true posterior p(z|x), and introduce amortized variational inference q_phi(z|x).
objectives.group: Latent variable formulations & the ELBO derivation

objectives.text: Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO): Derive the mathematical ELBO from Jensen's inequality: log p(x) >= E[log p(x|z)] - D_KL(q(z|x) || p(z)), balancing reconstruction and prior regularization.
objectives.group: Latent variable formulations & the ELBO derivation

objectives.text: Reparameterization Trick: Derive backpropagation through stochastic sampling nodes by decomposing latent variables as z = mu + sigma * epsilon where epsilon ~ N(0, I).
Latent Space Disentanglement: Implement beta-VAE to scale the KL regularization penalty and evaluate factorized, disentangled latent representation dimensions.

modules.mentalModel: A VAE maps complex high-dimensional data into a continuous, smooth low-dimensional latent manifold where every point can be decoded into a realistic sample.

modules.name: Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) & Minimax Dynamics

objectives.group: Two-player zero-sum games & the minimax objective

objectives.text: Divergence Minimization: Prove that under an optimal discriminator, the minimax game minimizes the Jensen-Shannon Divergence between true and generated distributions.
objectives.group: Two-player zero-sum games & the minimax objective

objectives.text: Training Instabilities: Analyze mode collapse, vanishing gradients under optimal discriminators, and cyclic non-convergence limit cycles.
Wasserstein GAN with Gradient Penalty: Derive the Earth Mover's Distance via Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality, enforce 1-Lipschitz continuity with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP).

modules.mentalModel: A GAN is an adversarial arms race; the discriminator provides an adaptive, learnable loss function that guides the generator to match the real data manifold.
modules.tryIt: Train a WGAN-GP on an image dataset, plot the continuous Wasserstein loss critic curves, and verify that it avoids the mode collapse failure of a standard vanilla GAN.
modules.outcome: You can formulate adversarial games, implement Wasserstein GANs with gradient penalty, and diagnose training instabilities.
modules.evidence: Train a WGAN-GP on an image dataset, plot the continuous Wasserstein loss critic curves, and verify that it avoids the mode collapse failure of a standard vanilla GAN.

modules.name: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM) & Score-Based SDEs

objectives.text: Forward Gaussian Markov Chain: Formulate the forward process adding scheduled Gaussian noise beta_1...beta_T; derive closed-form sampling of x_t directly from x_0 at any step t.
Reverse Denoising Process: Parameterize the reverse mean using a neural network predicting the injected noise epsilon_theta(x_t, t) under the simplified MSE variational bound.
Score-Based Perspective: Unify diffusion with Score-Based Generative Modeling (Song et al.) via continuous Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs) and Probability Flow ODEs.
Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG): Implement unconditional label dropout during training and scale conditional score estimates during inference to trade diversity for sample quality.

modules.mentalModel: Diffusion gradually dissolves data structure into pure Gaussian chaos, then trains a neural network to systematically reverse entropy step by step.
modules.tryIt: Code a 1D or 2D toy diffusion model from scratch in PyTorch, implement the analytical closed-form forward sampling, and visualize the reverse denoising trajectory over 1,000 steps.
modules.outcome: You can derive forward and reverse diffusion processes, implement DDPM training and sampling loops, and apply Classifier-Free Guidance.
modules.evidence: Code a 1D or 2D toy diffusion model from scratch in PyTorch, implement the analytical closed-form forward sampling, and visualize the reverse denoising trajectory over 1,000 steps.

modules.name: Continuous Flow Matching (CFM) & Optimal Transport Paths

objectives.text: Change of Variables: Formulate finite normalizing flows via invertible mappings and Jacobian determinants; transition to Continuous-Time Normalizing Flows (CNFs).
Neural ODEs: Model continuous probability trajectories using parameterized time-dependent velocity vector fields: dx/dt = v_theta(x, t).
Vector Field Regression: Formulate Flow Matching (Lipman et al.) to regress vector fields directly without expensive numerical ODE integration during training.
objectives.group: Flow matching & Optimal Transport probability paths

objectives.text: Optimal Transport Flow Matching (OT-CFM): Construct straight probability trajectories between Gaussian noise and target data distributions, enabling fast ODE generation in 10-20 steps.
objectives.group: Flow matching & Optimal Transport probability paths

modules.mentalModel: Flow Matching learns straight, deterministic vector fields that push pure noise into complex data manifolds without the curved, stochastic paths of diffusion.
modules.tryIt: Train an Optimal Transport Flow Matching model on a 2D multimodal distribution, solve the reverse trajectory with an explicit Euler ODE solver, and compare steps vs diffusion.
modules.outcome: You can formulate continuous-time neural ODEs, implement Optimal Transport Flow Matching, and sample high-quality generations with fast numerical solvers.
modules.evidence: Train an Optimal Transport Flow Matching model on a 2D multimodal distribution, solve the reverse trajectory with an explicit Euler ODE solver, and compare steps vs diffusion.

modules.name: Policy Gradients, Actor-Critic & Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)

objectives.text: Policy Optimization: Formulate parameterized stochastic policies pi_theta(a|s) and derive the Policy Gradient Theorem: grad J(theta) = E[grad log pi_theta(a|s) * Q(s, a)].
Variance Reduction: Implement the REINFORCE algorithm with state-value baseline subtraction to reduce Monte Carlo gradient variance without introducing bias.
Actor-Critic Architecture: Implement Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C), simultaneously learning policy actor pi_theta and value function critic V_phi to compute advantage A(s, a).
PPO Clipped Objective: Formulate Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), clipping probability ratios r_t(theta) to prevent destructive policy updates while avoiding TRPO constraints.

modules.mentalModel: Policy gradients directly climb the expected reward surface; PPO constrains policy updates to a trusted proximal region to guarantee stable monotonic improvement.
modules.tryIt: Implement PPO from scratch in PyTorch, verify that the clipped surrogate objective prevents catastrophic policy collapse, and evaluate training reward curves.
modules.outcome: You can derive the Policy Gradient Theorem, implement Actor-Critic algorithms, and configure PPO for continuous and discrete action spaces.

modules.name: Cross-Disciplinary Research Translation & Real-World Validation

objectives.text: Interdisciplinary Co-Design: Partner with clinicians, cybersecurity analysts, structural biologists, or climate scientists to translate domain workflows into mathematical formulations.
Ground Truth Discrepancies: Identify discrepancies between clinical/domain reality and naive machine learning labels, avoiding surrogate metric fallacies.
Clinical AI Standards: Adhere to reporting guidelines (CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT-AI) and regulatory frameworks (FDA AI/ML Software as a Medical Device / SaMD guidance).
Prospective vs Retrospective Evidence: Differentiate retrospective historical benchmark evaluation from prospective clinical trials and shadow-deployment user studies.

modules.mentalModel: In applied domain research, domain experts define clinical or scientific validity; model accuracy on an artificial benchmark is meaningless if it optimizes the wrong clinical proxy.

modules.name: Selecting a High-Impact Thesis Topic & Gap Identification

objectives.text: The Venn Diagram of Thesis Topic Selection: Intersect personal intellectual curiosity, advisor expertise and grant funding, available compute and data resources, and community urgency.

White Space Mapping: Construct an exhaustive literature taxonomy to uncover genuine white spaces in contemporary AI research that have been overlooked or prematurely abandoned.
Resource & Feasibility Audits: Calculate total required GPU compute hours, dataset access barriers, and institutional permissions before committing multi-year doctoral effort.

modules.mentalModel: A thesis topic is a multi-year investment of your intellectual career; choosing an overcrowded or resource-infeasible problem guarantees frustration and low impact.

Downscaled Proof-of-Concepts: Execute downscaled experiments on synthetic data or subsampled benchmarks (e.g. 10% data on single GPU) to verify signal presence.
Signal-to-Noise Evaluation: Evaluate pilot results to determine whether the proposed mechanism yields sufficient empirical effect size to justify full-scale investigation.

objectives.text: The Thesis Pivot Protocol: Execute a formal pivot when pilot evidence fails to confirm the hypothesis, salvaging theoretical insights and redirecting methodology.

modules.name: Research Paper Writing: The Anatomy of a Top-Tier Manuscript

objectives.text: The 5-Sentence Abstract: Draft abstracts following the structured template: Context -> Problem -> Identified Gap -> Proposed Solution -> Primary Quantitative Finding.
objectives.group: Titles, abstracts & the introduction sales funnel

objectives.text: The Introduction Funnel: Structure paper introductions as a persuasive funnel: broad domain significance -> why existing approaches fail -> core scientific insight -> explicit list of bulleted novel contributions.
objectives.group: Titles, abstracts & the introduction sales funnel

objectives.text: Mathematical Formalization: Present algorithms using formal mathematical notation, explicit objective functions, and pseudo-code algorithm blocks.
Experimental Section Writing: Author crystal-clear experimental setup sections, baseline configurations, and detailed reproducibility checklists.
Limitations & Broader Impact: Write transparent limitations and broader societal impact statements that preempt skeptical reviewer criticisms.

modules.mentalModel: A research paper is not a chronological diary of what you did in the lab; it is an optimized, logical argument designed to convince a skeptical reviewer of a specific new truth.
modules.tryIt: Rewrite the introduction and abstract of an existing research paper into the 5-sentence abstract framework and introduction funnel, ensuring every contribution is explicitly claimed.
modules.outcome: You can draft compelling, mathematically rigorous scientific manuscripts that structure arguments to maximize reviewer comprehension and enthusiasm.

objectives.group: Premier computer science conferences vs archival journals

objectives.text: Premier Archival Journals: Evaluate flagship journals: IEEE TPAMI, Journal of Machine Learning Research (JMLR), Nature Machine Intelligence, Nature Communications, IEEE TNNLS, and ACM Computing Surveys.
objectives.group: Premier computer science conferences vs archival journals

objectives.group: Premier computer science conferences vs archival journals

objectives.group: Spotting and avoiding predatory journals & paper mills

objectives.text: The Think-Check-Submit Protocol: Audit candidate journals against Beall's List criteria, verifying legitimate indexing in Web of Science, Scopus, DBLP, and Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ).
objectives.group: Spotting and avoiding predatory journals & paper mills

objectives.text: Red Flag Detection: Recognize fake metrics ("Global Impact Factor", "Universal Impact Factor"), fake editorial boards, unsolicited spam email solicitations, and implausible 48-hour acceptance promises.
objectives.group: Spotting and avoiding predatory journals & paper mills

modules.name: Peer Review Mastery, Author Rebuttals & Reviewer Response Tables

objectives.text: Peer Review Mechanics: Understand the roles of Area Chairs (AC), Senior Metareviewers, and Reviewers; deconstruct reviewer scoring rubrics (Novelty, Soundness, Rigor, Clarity).
objectives.group: The peer review process from the inside

objectives.text: The Reviewer Mindset: Recognize reviewer cognitive biases: fatigue, skimming under tight deadlines, anchoring on minor flaws, and defensive skepticism toward radical claims.
objectives.group: The peer review process from the inside

objectives.text: The Psychology of Effective Rebuttals: Maintain an objective, appreciative, and respectful tone, avoiding defensive rhetoric or dismissive confrontation.
Point-by-Point Response Tables: Construct structured response dossiers: [Reviewer Query] -> [Author Clarification] -> [Concrete Action Taken & Exact Line Numbers in Revised Draft].
Emergency Rebuttal Experiments: Design, execute, and report requested baseline comparisons and ablation experiments within tight 1-week conference rebuttal windows.

modules.mentalModel: A peer review rebuttal is not a debate you win by arguing; it is an objective evidentiary hearing where you provide data, code, and revisions that address reviewer concerns.
